key_insight: Non-Gaussian bosonic input states can achieve positive coherent information — and hence positive quantum capacity — in thermal-loss regimes where all single-mode Gaussian states fail.
engineering_relevance: This identifies higher-noise operating regimes where continuous-variable quantum links may still be viable, broadening design targets for bosonic quantum communication hardware.
method: Proved the classic Holevo–Werner thermal-state lower bound is optimal over all single-mode Gaussian inputs.
Constructed an explicit rank-two non-Gaussian state over six Fock levels with certified positive coherent information.
Compared certified witnesses with numerical optimization over non-Gaussian families to map the feasible noise/transmissivity region.
evidence_signal: At environment thermal photon number ν=1 and transmissivity η=0.8, all single-mode Gaussian inputs give non-positive coherent information, while a six-level non-Gaussian witness certifies at least 4.7×10^-4 qubits/use and numerical searches reach 8.4×10^-3; positivity is certified down to η=0.7841.
watch_item: The explicit certified gains are small and the best-performing inputs are non-Gaussian and finite-dimensional in the Fock basis, so practical state preparation and loss-sensitive implementation may be challenging.
paper_title: Bosonic quantum communication beyond the thermal threshold
